forecaster_note: Clean chest to head high surf at the S magnets, with another pulse of S swell expected later. The shorter-period S swell has eased further, but mid and long-period S fills in through the day. Clean all morning under light offshores, then NE sea breezes turn things bumpy to lumpy for most — S-facing corners stay cleanish. (Surfline Sydney forecast team, 20 Sep 2026.)

wind.summary: WNW offshore hanging on another hour or two, then a light NE sea breeze from around midday; gusty W kick near dusk.

shark.summary: Active: SLSNSW drone sighted a shark at Freshwater Beach at 7:22am today. Also overnight, tagged white shark #2373 pinged the North Narrabeen receiver at 10:04pm (19 Sep). Dee Why sits between the two — nothing logged on its own beach, but keep your head up.

days.label: Today
days.note: Small but clean and the offshore is still holding at 9am — you've got maybe two hours before the NE sea breeze puts bump on it. Thigh-to-waist everywhere. Swell is dead S at 185 degrees so Dee Why is wrapping poorly; Long Reef and Curl Curl hold the better shape. Hot one today, 28C by noon. Note the shark alert at Freshwater this morning.

dee-why.window: Now until ~11:30am, before the NE breeze
alerts: Dead-S swell at 185° — wraps badly into Dee Why, soft lined-up walls rather than punch

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: The Point right is your frontside wall but it's starved at this angle. The beachie banks down the south end will have more push this morning.

long-reef.window: Now until ~11:30am — pick of the four this morning

tip.label: Frontside walls
tip.text: Best angle of the four for this S swell. Sit wide on the point and take the frontside rights — they'll run further than anything at Dee Why today.

alerts: 🦈 Tagged white shark detected at North Narrabeen receiver 10:04pm last night

tip.label: Work the south end
tip.text: S swell into the south corner gives the cleanest banks. Rights off the peaks are your frontside; the lefts are short backside sections.

tip.text: Only worth it if you're already in Manly. North Steyne banks need more east in the swell than today's dead S.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Dawn is the whole story. Longer-period S swell still running with chest-to-head sets at the south magnets under offshore NW, then a southerly change pushes through Sydney around 9-10am and turns everything lumpy and onshore for the rest of the day. Be in the water by 6:30am or don't bother.
